newsitem.title: USA: KCBT July wheat jumps to 10-1/2 month high.
newsitem.headline: KCBT July wheat jumps to 10-1/2 month high.

text.p: KCBT new crop hard red winter July wheat surged to a new 10-1/2-month high and all months closed sharply higher on escalating concerns that a large amount of wheat was lost in last week's freeze in the U.S. Great Plains, traders said.
"The momentum of the story goes back above 200 million bushels lost," a trader said.

July touched a session high of $4.84 per bushel, the highest level for that month since $4.87 was notched on May 24, 1996. The contract high for July is $4.99 which was set a year ago on April 22, 1996.
Crop experts Friday again expressed ideas that a lot of wheat has been damaged.

Last week's freeze may have sliced more than 100 million bushels from the Kansas wheat crop and severe losses in Oklahoma also were likely, said crop specialists in those states. In Kansas alone, last week's freeze may have cut production 100 million to 150 million bushels.

"Those numbers for Kansas alone are not unrealistic," said Rollie Sears, a Kansas State University wheat breeder, who this week toured the damaged areas. "The damage in the southern third of the state is worse than I thought."
Thursday's EU decision to halt EU weekly wheat export tenders amid mounting concerns about dry weather plus a forecast for more dry weather in France, boosted prices.
French weather forecasters Friday predicted another five days without rain across most of the country's farm districts.
KCBT wheat futures volume was estimated at 61.850 million bushels, above the 56.735 million traded Thursday.
KCBT wheat closed three to 20 cents per bushel higher, with May up 17-1/2 at $4.99-1/2 a bushel and July was 18-1/4 higher at $4.81.
